blocks.content: The apiVersion field, seen at the top of literally every manifest throughout this course, follows a consistent group/version structure, this topic makes that structure explicit.
Most apiVersion values follow the pattern group/version, the API group a resource belongs to, followed by which version of that group's API you are targeting.

blocks.alt: A consistent, two-part structure, underlying every apiVersion value you have written

blocks.content: 2. The Core Group Has No Prefix
blocks.text: 2. The Core Group Has No Prefix

blocks.content: This is worth calling out explicitly, since it looks like an exception, the original, "core" API group (Pods, Services, ConfigMaps, and other foundational types) uses no group prefix at all, just v1, exactly what every Pod and Service manifest in this course has used.

blocks.alt: The one genuine exception, and exactly what every Pod manifest in this course has used

blocks.content: Everything added after Kubernetes's earliest days lives in a named group, apps/v1 for Deployments and StatefulSets, batch/v1 for Jobs, networking.k8s.io/v1 for Ingress, exactly the values used consistently throughout this course.

blocks.alt: Named groups, exactly the values you have already seen used consistently throughout this course

blocks.content: The version portion also signals maturity, v1alpha1 (experimental, can change or disappear), v1beta1 (more stable, still evolving), and plain v1 (stable, safe to depend on long-term), a real, meaningful convention worth reading before adopting a newer feature.

blocks.alt: A real signal about stability, worth reading before depending on something newer

blocks.content: kubectl explain tells you exactly the correct apiVersion for any given Kind, directly from your own cluster, rather than guessing or relying on possibly outdated documentation.

blocks.alt: A direct, authoritative answer from your own cluster, not a guess

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: apiVersion follows a group/version structure, the core group uniquely has no prefix at all, just v1, everything else uses a named group like apps/v1.
The version itself signals maturity (alpha, beta, stable), and kubectl explain gives you the authoritative, correct value directly from your own cluster.
